description:
`me` lets an app you authorize read the parts of your UnitySVC profile you choose, and, only if you also allow it, update them.

The gateway answers `me` itself (`me://profile`): there is no upstream. A read returns exactly the profile paths the calling key's `service:me` grant lists in its `fields` option (a section such as `research`, or one value inside it such as `address.state`), served from your account's routing context, so whether a section is public plays no part. A write is forwarded to UnitySVC, which checks the grant and that the key's owner may edit the account, then merges the data into the section. `me` exports two permissions and nothing else: `read` and `write`. `invoke`, and the `service:*` and `*` wildcards that stand for it, never reach `me`. `fields` defaults to nothing, so a grant must list what it covers; `fields=*` (the whole profile) is for keys you create yourself, never for a key issued to another service. `me` is not billed.

Call `GET /me` for every permitted section, or `GET /me/<section>` for one, with a UnitySVC key whose policy grants `service:me` with `read`, e.g. `{"object": "service:me", "permissions": ["read"], "options": "fields=research,address.state"}`. To update a section, `POST /me` with `{"name": "<section>", "public": <bool>, "data": {...}}` using a key whose grant also holds `write` and lists that whole section. Edit your profile itself under **Profile** in the dashboard.

fields.description: Profile paths this grant covers: a section name (research), or a section followed by keys of its object data (address.state). A write needs the whole section listed. * is the whole profile, for keys you create yourself only. Unset covers nothing.

name: me

payout_price.description: Not billed: reading and updating your own profile is free

summary: Let an app read the parts of your UnitySVC profile you choose through `/me`, and update them only if you also allow it.
